o1.biggest_strength: Every email opens on the pricing change and the rev rec rebuild in a real finance person's voice, with list rules and reply-rate math that match the pilot exactly.
o1.biggest_mistake: It quotes the internal persona line almost verbatim and claims a one-page summary and 'three steps' will be sent without confirming those assets exist.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the exact asset behind each reply ask (the one-pager, the three steps) so nothing is promised that isn't written yet.

o2.biggest_strength: Tight, scannable structure with clean metric tables and a clear per-100-contacts projection.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 8% target (range 7-10%) invents a 1.25x lift multiplier the pilot never tested, inflating the expected reply rate above the 7.9% trigger ceiling.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use the pilot's own 6.8-7.9% band as the expectation and keep the invented uplift out of the forecast.

reason: Output 1 sounds more like a finance person talking to a finance person, keeps the proof as plain words, and gives an honest reply rate instead of a multiplied wish; Output 2's forecast math is clever but not something I'd defend to my team.
